steps.text: In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise, minced garlic, and lemon juice. Set aside in the refrigerator.
Preheat the grill for high heat.

Brush vegetables with olive oil on each side. Brush grate with oil. Place bell peppers and zucchini closest to the middle of the grill, and set onion and squash pieces around them. Cook for about 3 minutes, turn, and cook for another 3 minutes. The peppers may take a bit longer. Remove from grill, and set aside.

Spread some of the mayonnaise mixture on the cut sides of the bread, and sprinkle each one with feta cheese. Place on the grill cheese side up, and cover with lid for 2 to 3 minutes. This will warm the bread, and slightly melt the cheese. Watch carefully so the bottoms don't burn. Remove from grill, and layer with the vegetables. Enjoy as open faced grilled sandwiches.

raw_recipe.headline: California Grilled Veggie Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: For a smoky and sumptuous veggie-filled grilled sandwich, try this easy recipe. All it takes is some veggies, focaccia bread, lemon-mayonnaise dressing, and crumbled feta.
raw_recipe.name: California Grilled Veggie Sandwich

review.reviewBody: Trust me, you will not miss the meat in this sandwich! I also broiled my veggies because of the snow outside on top of the grill. The only veggie I added was green pepper only because I had one. I will use a large red onion next time because we love the carmelized flavor of the onion under the broiler. I also sprayed my veggies with balsamic vinegar for some extra "zip". Served the veggies on hearty multi-grain rolls from Whole Foods - - use the best bread possible because it truly will make or break the sandwich. Excellent recipe, Heather!!

This was REALLY delicious! As others suggested, I marinated the veggies beforehand and I think that turned out to be a smart move. I bought 1 zucchini, 1 yellow squash, about half of a sweet red pepper and about 8 stalks of asparagus. I tossed them with 3 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper. I marinated them in the fridge for about 45 minutes, stirring them occasionally. Because it's a bit cold here today, I roasted the vegetables instead of grilling them: about 20 minutes at 450deg (stirring halfway). I then put the sauce on the rolls, then some shredded mozzarella and shredded parmesan, and put them under the broiler for a minute or two. The sauce with the marinade was really quite delicious. I will cut back on the oil next time because 3 tbsp was a bit too much for that amount of vegetables. I can't wait to try this again!

I roasted the veggies in the oven under the broiler, and used tandoori naan instead of focaccia since the store didn’t have any. I assembled the sandwiches and toasted them in a skillet with a little bit of non-stick spray. Yummy!

Absolutely delishus! I used my Rachel Ray grill pan (as I don't have a real grill) and the veggies came out tasty; I bought focaccia bread from Panera's, cut into 1/4s, and each in 1/2. I used Italian seasoning in the mayo dressing as I was out of garlic cloves and yellow squash. I added green and yellow thinly sliced peppers and minced mozzarella instead of feta. WOW! I recommend this filling dish even for a light dinner.

Amazing! This has become an easy and delicious staple. I add balsamic to the olive oil as suggested by others. Roasting in the oven works just as well as grilling (better even, I think it's faster). Worth it to take the care to cut the veggies into even chunks to avoid burned edges. Sauce is awesome, I've started using it in bagel sandwiches too. I've learned focaccia molds fast, but I just used my first frozen and microwave thawed piece and it still tasted great.

This recipe was great. I couldn't find regular focaccia bread, so I got herb & cheese focaccia and it worked quite well. I also didn't have a grill so I put the basted veggies in a glass Pyrex dish and broiled them under high heat, tossing them around every few minutes until they were cooked. I toasted the focaccia using the same method. Everything turned out great, this is an awesome recipe.

Fantastic! Hubby and son both loved it. So did I, so this recipe is a keeper for us. First of all: I have a large square grill pan for the stovetop, which I used for this recipe. One pan to do the whole thing. I followed the recipe but for the focaccia, I purchased individual buns (triangle-shaped). I sliced them in half to make sandwiches. I followed the instructions in the recipe about putting the bread on the grill (or in the pan, in my case) with the sauce and the feta, except that I did that with each bottom slice, then just placed the top halves on top. I covered that loosely and watched it so as not to overheat, then everything came out nice and warm. Then, after adding the veggies, everyone got a sandwich, a very filling one!

So good! The first time I made it I had used goat cheese. Mistake. The other times, I used grated parmesan cheese. Yum. Also used Costco's ciabatta rolls. Poured some oil on cookie sheet, spread thin with a paper towel. Put the veges on pan. Put a thin layer of a balsamic glaze (Costco online) on veges. Broiled on second level from top, about 5 min. Flipped, added another thin layer of balsamic glaze. Baked another 5 min. FYI- I put the onion on a separate cookie sheet and broiled first; then took it out and put the vege cookie sheet in it's place; at the same time I then put the onion cookie sheet back in the oven, but on the rack below the veges. (To keep warm and cook a little more.)

This was excellent! I was looking for something meatless for tonight and this is what I happened upon, and am so glad to have found it! Thank you Heather! My changes: I used generous slices of a hearty whole grain bread; added tomatoes and basil to the veggie mix and marinated in olive oil and balsamic vinegar for about 30 minutes, then baked veggies in a 400 degree oven for about 20 minutes. Assembled sandwiches according to individual veggie preferences, topped with a wee bit more feta and put under the broiler just long enough to melt the cheese. Served with a caesar salad. Delicious! This is about to become a staple in my house!

Delicious sandwich! Super filling, my husband and I didn't miss the meat at all. Since I am not a fan of squash, I used egg plant instead, added sliced portobello mushrooms and marinated artichoke hearts. Marinated the veggies in balsamic vinaigrette dressing over night as suggested by other reviews, and replaced the feta with provolone (my husband isn't a fan of feta). It was one of the best sandwiches we have had and will be a regular on our menu from now on.

This was a fantastic sandwich. Instead of the garlic I added some pesto paste for added flavor to the mayo and lemon juice.
I also put the ciabatta roll on the grill with some shredded mozzarella to let it get warm before topping with vegetables. Excellent !! Will absolutely make this again!

Yum. Added an eggplant. Great way to use CSA vegetables. Added an eggplant and increased the olive oil due to my abundance of veggies, but only added 1 tbsp balsamic, s&p, and broiled. Would crisp bread in oven, then add mayo and cheese before topping with veggies. Have enough to freeze and use later for more sandwiches, a side for chicken, or in an omelette or frittata.
Delicious and hearty! Even my 12 year old and 15 year old daughter love these. Our family likes to double the sauce!
Delicious! Mine was not as pretty as in the photo, but we loved the flavors!!
This sandwich is delicious! My husband said this recipe is a keeper.
This recipe is delicious. Very easy to make and healthy. The combination of all these ingredients with the mayo spread makes it very tasty. I loved it.

Amazing. We’re trying to get more veggies in our diet. This is a delicious way to do it. Skipped the bread and roasted the veggies in oven instead of grilling. Put the cooked veggies in a bowl and topped with feta and the delicious lemon garlic Mayo. WOW! Hubby said “keep this recipe!”
Pleasantly surprised at how good it turned out. Made sourdough focaccia To go with grilled vegetables. Will definitely make it again.
Very good. I roasted the veggies vs. grilling and sandwich was delicious.

I loved this! A great way to eat a bunch of veggies!

I used a rosemary bread loaf as I couldn't find foccacia. Also used some goat cheese when I used up all the feta (it was amazing!) Since I didn't have the mayo on hand, I used a spinach dip I had in the fridge for the base- it was great!
